title: Establish degradable-resilience SLO matrix with phased regional evacuation and adaptive circuit-breaker tiers
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: define a pragmatic, operational SLO/SLI schema for conversational and generation endpoints that supports graceful degradation (quality-first -> latency-first) and explicit multi-region evacuation windows. This ticket captures definitions, burn thresholds, circuit-breaker tiers, and a phased evacuation/runbook that the SLO arbiter and routing tier will implement.

Background: after the 2026-01 multi-region incident we observed customers experiencing sudden quality regressions and token-price spikes when regional capacity was constrained. Our existing SLO surface is per-endpoint availability/latency only; we need a richer, per-endpoint and per-model matrix that can express degradable quality levels, token-weighted SLI attribution, and staged evacuation holdbacks to avoid cascading capacity failures.

Success criteria (measurable):
- Published SLO matrix covering short-turn chat, long-form generation, and embedding routes with SLI formulas.
- Automated arbiter rules that trigger progressive actions (soft-shed low-priority tokens -> switch to quantized variant -> regional evacuation -> route-level circuit breaker) with observable runbook steps.
- Dashboards showing error budget burn, predicted burn-rate, and last-24h mitigation actions.
- One end-to-end tabletop that validates the playbook for a regional capacity event.

Proposed SLI / SLO primitives (per route):
- Success-rate SLI: fraction of requests that return a 2xx with model-generated content and no upstream retry, measured at request granularity.
- Latency SLI: p95 request-to-first-token (RTFT) and p99 request completion time; SLOs defined per route class.
- Quality SLI (daily): periodic eval pass-rate against a route-specific promptset (monthly baseline) used for rollout gates and long-term error budget recovery.
- Token-weighted availability: availability weighted by tokens consumed (important for long-gen routes).

Example target matrix (initial rollout):
- chat.short (interactive): Success-rate SLO 99.5% (rolling 30d), p95 RTFT < 250ms (rolling 7d), error-budget policy: day-burn alert if 24h burn-rate > 3x.
- gen.long (document generation): Success-rate SLO 99.0% (30d), p95 completion < 1200ms, token-weighted availability SLO 99.2%.
- embeddings: Success-rate SLO 99.9% (30d), p99 latency < 150ms.

Error budget burn policy (coarse):
- Green: burn-rate <= 1.0. Normal operations, no mitigation.
- Amber: 1.0 < burn-rate <= 2.5. Trigger throttling of non-critical background jobs and start aggressive caching suggestions; notify on-call and PM.
- Red: burn-rate > 2.5. Start progressive mitigations: (1) soft-shed best-effort traffic (routes labeled low-priority), (2) route-specific autoscale overrides, (3) promote lower-cost quantized model variant for new requests, (4) if burn persists open regional evacuation.

Adaptive circuit-breaker tiers (per-route):
- Tier 1 (soft): trip on 1 minute error-rate > 10% OR p99 RTFT > 5s. Action: reject with 429 to non-critical tokens and surface diagnostic header X-RD-TRIP=soft. Auto-close after 1 minute if metrics recover.
- Tier 2 (hard): trip on 5 minute sustained error-rate > 7% OR sustained token-weighted burn causing region-level quota exhaustion. Action: open circuit for 5 minutes, redirect traffic to fallback model variant and fallthrough to alternate region where available.
- Tier 3 (evacuation): trigger when aggregated regional capacity forecast shows < 20% healthy capacity for > 10 minutes AND error budget is Red across >=2 critical routes. Action: coordinated phased evacuation (see runbook) with holdback windows for pinned tenants.

Phased regional evacuation (runbook summary):
1) Pre-evac check (automated): confirm region-level capacity forecast, model cache hit-rate drop, and burn-rate > 2.5.
2) Soft-evac (automated): route-level traffic steering to alternate region for low-priority/opt-in tenants; maintain a 10% soak in primary region for control.
3) Quantize (automated/manual rollback trigger): switch new requests to quantized variant for all non-P0 routes.
4) Pinned tenant holdback (manual review): reduce traffic for pinned tenants using traffic-capping API; notify solutions/sales.
5) Full-evac (manual): stop scheduling new inference in region, drain KV caches, and redirect stateful workloads.

Tradeoffs considered:
- User experience vs reliability: aggressive shedding reduces quality for some customers but prevents platform-wide outages. We prioritize pinned enterprise tenants via holdback windows.
- Complexity: per-route token-weighted SLIs add implementation complexity in telemetry pipelines; we propose a phased instrumentation plan (begin with chat.short and embeddings).
- Cost: promoting quantized variants reduces per-token cost but can degrade quality; use quality SLI signal to space how long quantized variants stay in place.

Open decisions (action items):
- Finalize thresholds for tier trips (assigned to Marcus Liu) by 2026-03-12.
- Instrument token-weighted availability in metrics pipeline (dependency ENG-314159).
- Add pinned-tenant holdback API (dependency ENG-271401).
